articles.originalTitle: Eight Dead, 18 Injured in Brooklyn Building Collapse Next to Construction Site - Engineering News-Record
articles.title: Eight People Killed After Brooklyn Building Collapses Next to Construction Site
articles.excerpt: In Brooklyn, New York, eight people, including two children and two construction workers, died after a three-story building collapsed next to an excavation site.
articles.content: In Brooklyn, New York, a three-story building collapsed into an adjoining construction excavation site on November 11, resulting in eight fatalities and 18 injuries. Firefighters concluded rescue operations on Thursday afternoon, while local authorities launched an investigation into the incident. Project records reviewed after the collapse showed that geotechnical reports had warned that excavation and related vibrations could adversely affect abutting structures, prescribing underpinning and monitoring thresholds. A preconstruction survey conducted in March had documented visible cracking and rated the north masonry facade in poor condition. Approved support-of-excavation plans detailed staged shoring systems and established movement limits that required work to halt if specific thresholds were exceeded. Following the disaster, the mayor ordered safety inspections at approximately 100 other construction sites associated with the involved companies, and the district attorney's office participated in the ongoing investigation.

articles.originalTitle: Designers’ Creative Freedom Unveiled at Molteni Museum Exhibit - WWD
articles.title: Molteni Museum Exhibition Unveils Unbridled Designer Creativity
articles.excerpt: The newly opened exhibition in Giussano features expressive works by prominent architects and designers, using existing Molteni Group furniture pieces as a starting point without commercial constraints.
articles.content: The Molteni Museum located in the Molteni Compound in Giussano, Italy, opened a new exhibition granting prominent designers creative freedom away from commercial constraints by using existing Molteni Group, UniFor and Citterio products as a foundation. Israeli artist Ron Gilad stated that the initiative was designed to let living creatives speak freely. The exhibition features works from Herzog & de Meuron, Jean Nouvel, Naoto Fukasawa, OMA, AMDL Circle, Foster + Partners Industrial Design, Patricia Urquiola, the late Luca Meda, and Vincent Van Duysen. Herzog & de Meuron reinterpreted the Porta Volta chair with candy-colored inflatable cushions, while Ron Gilad transformed Luca Meda kitchen design into a poetic fountain with four faucets. OMA adopted a surreal approach through material experimentation on the Principles table collection, and AMDL Circle re-imagined the MDL System with centipede-like contours. Video installations documenting the research and craftsmanship accompany the physical objects. The exhibition will remain on display for one year at the museum before embarking on an international tour.

articles.originalTitle: Berkshire Glade by Turkel Design - Architectural Record
articles.title: Turkel Design Completes Berkshire Glade Residence in Western Massachusetts
articles.excerpt: Situated in the Berkshire hills of Western Massachusetts, Berkshire Glade by Turkel Design functions as a multigenerational vacation home and future full-time residence. The 6,510-square-foot property comprises two distinct volumes joined by a covered porch.
articles.content:
Designed by Turkel Design, Berkshire Glade is located in the Berkshire hills of Western Massachusetts and overlooks a tree-lined hillside with views of Mount Washington. Spanning 6,510 square feet, the property serves as both a multigenerational vacation home and a future full-time residence for a couple whose careers span New York City and Boston.

The residential project consists of two distinct volumes, a primary residence and a guest house, joined by a covered porch anchored by a fireplace. The engineered-wood structure utilizes natural materials including Douglas fir glue-laminated beams and thermally modified hemlock. The exterior is clad in shou sugi ban, a Japanese charred wood resistant to rot and insects. Components including exterior and interior wall systems, roof and floor systems, windows, doors, flooring, and custom built-in cabinetry were fabricated as a package in a climate-controlled facility before being shipped to the site for precision assembly. The project was completed in May 2025.

articles.originalTitle: Crosslam completes Brazil’s tallest mass-timber tower - Dezeen
articles.title: Brazil's Tallest Mass-Timber Hybrid Tower Completed in São Paulo
articles.excerpt: Engineering firm Crosslam has completed Aurora 275, a hybrid timber building in São Paulo that is the tallest of its type in Brazil. Standing 22 meters tall, the structure was built to demonstrate mass-timber potential to the local market.
articles.content: Engineering firm Crosslam has designed and built Aurora 275, a hybrid timber building located in the Suzano area of São Paulo, which the company states is the tallest of its type in Brazil. Standing 22 meters tall, Aurora 275 features a structural system consisting of a reinforced concrete core, metal elements, and mass-timber components including glulam beams and columns and cross-laminated timber floorplates. Crosslam, which typically acts as an engineer for other firms, designed the building to demonstrate the viability of mass timber and build trust within the Brazilian market. Constructed in four weeks by a five-person team, the building utilizes timber sourced within Brazil. The structure features a metal-clad facade with yellow detailing and includes balconies for its 10 apartments. Interior spaces expose the timber elements to provide a warm aesthetic. According to the project team, engineered timber offers construction advantages such as faster assembly, dimensional precision, reduced site waste, a lighter structure, and lower carbon emissions. The company claimed the building is carbon neutral.

articles.originalTitle: SITE Santa Fe Announces Theme and Artist List for 13th International Biennial - ARTnews.com
articles.title: SITE Santa Fe Announces Theme and Artist List for 13th Biennial
articles.excerpt: Ekow Eshun will curate the 13th International Biennial at SITE Santa Fe, opening next June. Titled "There Are Other Worlds," the exhibition will feature more than 40 artists.
articles.content: SITE Santa Fe in New Mexico has announced the theme and artist list for its 13th International Biennial, opening next June. Exhibition curator Ekow Eshun selected the title "There Are Other Worlds," a release stated, positing that other worlds already exist within our own through plain sight, refusal of the status quo, or imagination. The exhibition comprises 3 sections: "Worlds Beyond," informed in part by the Transcendental Painting Group; "World in Common," examining community and kinship; and "Worlds Alive," focusing on human, animal, and plant interdependence. More than 40 artists will exhibit across SITE Santa Fe and other venues in the city. Eshun commissioned new works from Edgar Arceneaux, Firelei Báez, Raven Chacon, Lotus L. Kang, and Cauleen Smith. Additional participating artists include John Akomfrah, Frank Bowling, Olafur Eliasson, Jeffrey Gibson, Nan Goldin, Delcy Morelos, Eamon Ore-Giron, Rose Simpson, and Sandra Vásquez de la Horra. Eshun stated that these practices share a sense that the world is continually reshaped by perception and imagination, inviting audiences to consider alternative ways of being.

articles.originalTitle: Biennale Arte 2026 | TAREK EL-ARISS | Emptying the Jars of War, or How We Learned to Love Nature - La Biennale di Venezia
articles.title: Tarek El-Ariss to Discuss War, Nature, and Water Politics at Biennale Arte 2026
articles.excerpt: Tarek El-Ariss will examine how crises alter perceptions of nature and reframe sustainability during a lecture at Biennale Arte 2026.
articles.content: Tarek El-Ariss is scheduled to speak at an event during Biennale Arte 2026 on November 21, 2026. Taking place at Teatro Piccolo Arsenale from 16:00 to 17:30, the lecture will be introduced and moderated by Rasha Salti. The session addresses how crises and wars not only damage the environment but also unsettle perceptions of nature. Drawing from everyday scenes such as saving water jars for bathing during wartime in Lebanon, the discussion traces longer histories and mythologies of water and greenery from the Garden of Eden to Greek and Islamic traditions, while focusing on the oasis as a recurring fantasy. The lecture posits that environmental practices do not necessarily emerge from ethical choices, often arising instead through habit, fear, or the quest for survival. Sustainability is reframed as a negotiation that interrogates the politics of purity and control to imagine alternative futures. Admission to the event is free until venue capacity is reached.

articles.originalTitle: FRIEDA EKOTTO | Resilience Against Value: Authored Practices of Repair in Otobong Nkanga and Ibrahim Mahama - La Biennale di Venezia
articles.title: Frieda Ekotto to Deliver Lecture at Teatro Piccolo Arsenale
articles.excerpt: Frieda Ekotto will deliver a lecture examining the repair practices in the works of Otobong Nkanga and Ibrahim Mahama. The event takes place on November 20, 2026, at Teatro Piccolo Arsenale.
articles.content: Frieda Ekotto will present a lecture examining the gathering, wrapping, repairing, and regenerating actions central to the practices of Otobong Nkanga and Ibrahim Mahama. The event is scheduled for November 20, 2026, from 16:00 to 17:30 at Teatro Piccolo Arsenale. The discussion explores processes that redirect materials, labor, and time toward connections between land, body, and community that extraction seeks to disrupt. These actions form a resilience rooted in acts of refusal. By framing disobedience as the foundation of resilience, the lecture recasts the work of both artists as a sustained challenge to damaging value systems, pointing toward a relational model of authorship. Rasha Salti will introduce and moderate the session. Admission to the venue is free until capacity is reached.

articles.originalTitle: Liverpool Biennial Announces Artist List and ‘Age of Magical Thinking’ Theme - ARTnews.com
articles.title: Liverpool Biennial Announces 2027 Theme and Artist List
articles.excerpt: The 2027 Liverpool Biennial will run from June 5 to September 19 under the theme "The Age of Magical Thinking," inspired by Jean Piaget, featuring 25 artists and collectives across multiple venues.
articles.content: The 2027 edition of the Liverpool Biennial is scheduled to open on June 5 and run through September 19, featuring 25 artists and collectives under the theme "The Age of Magical Thinking." Curated by Aimee Harrison and Lucía Sanromán, the exhibition draws on psychologist Jean Piaget's concept of a childhood period where reality and make-believe blur, allowing imagination to help shape alternative worlds. The exhibition will span various venues across North West England, including the Bluecoat, FACT Liverpool, Walker Art Gallery, Open Eye Gallery, Victoria Gallery & Museum, Liverpool Cathedral, and the Exhibition Research Laboratory at Liverpool John Moores University. The program includes a public art project in Williamson Square created by local young people alongside artist Harold Offeh, as well as new commissioned works by Francis Alÿs, Tania Candiani, and Laakkuluk Williamson. Participating artists and collectives include Ad Minoliti, Amalia Pica, Anya Paintsil, Charmaine Poh, Dor Guez, EBB.Global, Elias Nafaa, Francis Alÿs, Harold Offeh, Hiroko Kubo, Immy Mali, Iván Argote, the vacuum cleaner, Laakkuluk Williamson, Wen Cheng Lee, Marilyn Boror Bor, Petrit Halilaj, Rineke Dijkstra, Robert Gabris, Ronak & Roza Moshtaghi, Ruth Ewan, Tania Candiani, Yarema Malashchuk, Roman Khimei, and Zohra Opoku.

articles.originalTitle: Loro Piana Celebrates Finest Cashmere, Stages Exhibition - WWD
articles.title: Loro Piana Awards 2025 Cashmere at New York Exhibition
articles.excerpt: Held in New York, the event celebrated cashmere measuring 12.89 microns in fineness and unveiled the Master of Cashmere exhibition highlighting the house's heritage.
articles.content: Loro Piana celebrated fiber fineness measuring 12.89 microns during the 2025 Loro Piana Cashmere of the Year Award ceremony held at The Brant Foundation in New York. The gathering also marked the opening of the Master of Cashmere exhibition, which showcases the Italian luxury house history and superior know-how. Company deputy chairman Pier Luigi Loro Piana noted that the award, established in 2015, reflects longstanding relationships with local communities built on trust and a shared commitment to quality. The 11th edition honored three couples of cashmere herders from Inner Mongolia, with the first-place prize awarded for 135.8 kg of greasy cashmere measuring 12.89 microns. A micron represents one-thousandth of a millimeter. Chief executive officer Frédéric Arnault emphasized that cashmere remains at the center of the brand identity, highlighting selective breeding efforts through The Loro Piana Method initiated in 2009 to preserve the Alashan goat. Arnault also pointed to the Resilient Threads project launched in Mongolia to support herders and local biodiversity in partnership with international organizations. Loro Piana continues its tradition of honoring fine raw materials globally, including the Record Bale Award for merino wool production in Australia and New Zealand.

articles.originalTitle: This Belgian designer’s home is a ‘winterised’ take on California modernism - Wallpaper*
articles.title: Belgian Designer Adapts California Modernism for Her Countryside Home
articles.excerpt: Belgian interior architect Bieke Casteleyn adapted California midcentury modernism to her country's cooler climate while designing her family residence.
articles.content: Located in a flat countryside area in Belgium, the residence stands as a winterized interpretation of California modernism. Set on a single level, the home pairs warm wood tones with abundant natural light, featuring grey-green exterior stones chosen to blend with the landscape and a grass-covered flat roof. Inside, main living areas are separated from the private wing by a sweeping corridor framed by glass walls. The designer balanced extensive glazing and long sightlines by incorporating warm tones, tactile textures, and organic curves. Rather than fitting furniture into a pre-existing layout, the interior was designed around a collection of vintage pieces, family antiques, and collectible designs. Thoughtful architectural touches, such as a circular roof opening for a growing tree and a deck overlooking a pond, deepen the connection to the surrounding natural environment.

articles.originalTitle: Venice exhibition tells the story of the man who brought together contemporary artists and Murano’s master glassblowers - The Art Newspaper
articles.title: Peggy Guggenheim Collection Exhibition Explores Egidio Costantini and Murano Glass
articles.excerpt: The Peggy Guggenheim Collection in Venice is hosting an exhibition examining entrepreneur Egidio Costantini's pioneering work in uniting contemporary artists with Murano glass masters.
articles.content: In 1952, Venetian entrepreneur Egidio Costantini conceived the idea of transforming contemporary artists' designs into artistic sculptures through collaboration with glassblowers on the island of Murano. Three years later, Costantini established the Fucina degli Angeli gallery to exhibit these experiments. Until the 1970s, he served as an interpreter between more than 100 international artists and Murano's master glassblowers. Opening this month at the Peggy Guggenheim Collection in Venice, a new exhibition tells the story of Fucina from the 1950s to the 1980s. Curated by art historian Cristina Beltrami, the exhibition displays over 100 works, including glass, paintings, and sculptures by luminaries such as Max Ernst, Oskar Kokoschka, Lucio Fontana, and Paul Jenkins, alongside previously unstudied archival material. The display also examines Peggy Guggenheim's vital backstage role in sustaining the gallery financially and facilitating European exhibitions. Costantini's collaborations with figures like Pablo Picasso and Jean Cocteau form a central part of the historical narrative. The exhibition runs from November 14 through March 29, 2027.

articles.originalTitle: Julia Stoschek Foundation to reopen Düsseldorf headquarters in 2027 - The Art Newspaper
articles.title: Julia Stoschek Foundation to Reopen Düsseldorf Headquarters in 2027
articles.excerpt: A month after closing its Berlin exhibition space, the Julia Stoschek Foundation announced it will reopen its Düsseldorf headquarters in April 2027 following renovations.
articles.content: Following the closure of its Berlin exhibition space in October, the nonprofit Julia Stoschek Foundation announced it will reopen its Düsseldorf headquarters in April 2027. The Düsseldorf space had closed for renovation in 2025. The inaugural exhibition in the revamped venue will feature works by 43 artists drawn from the foundation's collection, which focuses primarily on time-based art. Founder Julia Stoschek expressed joy at the collection's growth, noting that the Berlin location operated for 10 years before its closure as part of a strategic realignment. The reopening in Düsseldorf coincides with the foundation's 20th anniversary. Titled Selfish in Bed, the inaugural exhibition takes its name from a work by Sarah Lucas and will run from April 2027 to December 2027. It will include pieces by artists such as Wolfgang Tillmans, Bill Viola, Simon Fujiwara, Rosemarie Trockel, and Tracey Emin.

articles.originalTitle: 2026 Record Awards Winner: The Snake Building by C+S Architects - Architectural Record
articles.title: The Snake Building by C+S Architects Joins Belgian Regeneration Scheme
articles.excerpt: Designed by C+S Architects in Aarschot, Belgium, the four-story Snake Building comprises 29 units as part of a regeneration scheme on a former industrial site.
articles.content: Located in Aarschot, Belgium, the Snake Building is a multifamily housing project designed by C+S Architects as part of an urban regeneration scheme on a former industrial site. Rising from a J-shaped lot, the four-story development contains 29 residential units within a master plan coordinated by a2o Architekten. The building's massing features five gabled volumes separated by balcony gaps, echoing a traditional Flemish streetscape. Hand-laid long-format gray bricks clad the facade, punctuated by timber-framed windows. The ground level features retail storefronts oriented toward a landscaped plaza, while a rear courtyard facilitates daylighting and natural ventilation for terraces. Below grade, a parking garage serves the residents. Structural and MEP engineering for the project were carried out by Filip Van Den Voorde and Technieken respectively, with Dyls acting as client and general contractor.

articles.originalTitle: Constantinople to Istanbul: One City, Two Empires – exhibition large print guide - Victoria and Albert Museum
articles.title: Victoria and Albert Museum Examines the Dual Imperial History of Istanbul
articles.excerpt: The Victoria and Albert Museum has released an exhibition guide exploring the rich artistic traditions and historical evolution of Constantinople and Istanbul across two empires.
articles.content: Tracing the history of the city from Constantinople to Istanbul, the settlement was established as a capital when Roman Emperor Constantine I designated Byzantion as Nova Roma in 330 CE. Situated at the meeting point of Asia and Europe, the city served as the center of the Byzantine Empire until its fall in 1453, and subsequently as the Ottoman capital until 1922. A large print exhibition guide published by the Victoria and Albert Museum explores the architectural achievements and contrasting artistic traditions of the metropolis. While Byzantine Constantinople emphasized sacred images such as Christ Pantocrator in public and religious spaces, the Ottoman tradition favored text and calligraphy. The city's security relied on engineering feats including the 5.6-kilometer Theodosian Walls and the Aqueduct of Valens. Objects featured in the related research include ivory plaques, illuminated manuscripts, and precious stone cameos, illustrating the cosmopolitan fabric and diverse religious heritage preserved across sixteen centuries of imperial history.

articles.originalTitle: As war continues, local people mobilise to salvage southern Lebanon’s history - The Art Newspaper
articles.title: Local Communities Mobilize to Protect Heritage Amid Continuing Conflict in Southern Lebanon
articles.excerpt: As ongoing conflict and occupation affect southern Lebanon, local officials, residents, and organizations are racing to document and salvage historical buildings, religious sites, and cultural heritage amidst widespread destruction.
articles.content: Ongoing conflict and occupation in southern Lebanon continue to threaten historical structures, ancient monuments, groves, and cemeteries. Local officials, artists, and residents are attempting to preserve local history by scanning old buildings, recording oral history, and rescuing libraries. While Unesco has granted enhanced protection to 73 sites in Lebanon and inscribed five castles of Mount Amel on its World Heritage and danger lists in July, sites such as Beaufort, Dubieh, and Chama remain under occupation and have been affected by military activity. According to heritage organization Biladi founder Joanne Farchakh Bajjaly and regional director Ali Badawi, numerous villages, historical houses, religious sites, and cemeteries have been destroyed or severely damaged. Residents such as Riad Al-Assaad in Zrariyeh and artist Oussama Baalbaki in Odaisseh reported the destruction of their family homes and ancestral neighborhoods. Archaeological remains, ancient cemeteries, and centuries-old olive trees have also suffered extensive damage amidst the ongoing hostilities.

articles.originalTitle: jean nouvel’s shenzhen opera house takes shape on the waterfront, with completion set for 2028 - Designboom
articles.title: Shenzhen Opera House Takes Shape on Waterfront with 2028 Completion Target
articles.excerpt: Designed by Ateliers Jean Nouvel, the Shenzhen Opera House is taking shape along the Shekou waterfront in China. Featuring a curved roof evoking ocean waves, the cultural complex is targeted for completion in December 2028.
articles.content: Designed by Ateliers Jean Nouvel, the Shenzhen Opera House is under construction along the waterfront of Shekou in Shenzhen, China. Titled Light of the Sea, the cultural complex integrates a fluid roof, expansive public spaces, and four performance venues. Situated in Dongjiaotou with water surrounding three sides of the site, the Paris-based team proposed a sweeping curved roof evoking ocean waves. The program includes a 2,100-seat opera hall, an 1,800-seat concert hall, a 1,000-seat small opera hall, and a 500-seat multifunctional theater, complemented by public facilities, creative spaces, a stage production center, and performer accommodations. Acoustic design is a priority, targeting a background noise rating below NR 15, while construction incorporates digital design technologies alongside welding and surveying robots. The main auditorium integrates mother-of-pearl finishes along curved balconies and acoustic walls. The main roof structure is scheduled for completion in 2027, with overall project delivery targeted for December 2028.

articles.originalTitle: Miami Beach: Highlights - Art Basel
articles.title: Art Basel Miami Beach Showcases Digital Art and Contemporary Masterpieces
articles.excerpt: Taking place at a cultural crossroads in the Americas, Art Basel Miami Beach unites voices in contemporary art while highlighting new frontiers in digital creations.
articles.content: Art Basel Miami Beach presents a program that unites prominent voices in contemporary art alongside innovative presentations. The regional art fair brings together modern masterpieces and emerging talent on a single platform. The Zero 10 platform, dedicated to digital-era art, returns with Generation, its largest presentation to date. Curated by Karen Archey and Eli Scheinman, the exhibition spans 19 projects and explores connections between digital technologies and traditional art forms. Encompassing algorithmic art, immersive environments, painting, sculpture, and textiles, the presentation highlights works by creators such as Sarah Meyohas, Jon Rafman, and Studio Drift. Refik Anadol's collaboration with the Yawanawá community transforms Amazonian artwork, music, and weather data into evolving digital imagery. Meanwhile, Harm van den Dorpel draws on historical geometric drawings to produce generative pieces that unfold in real time during the event.

articles.originalTitle: Sumayya Vally Unveils First Permanent UAE Project With Dubai’s Elie Khouri Art Foundation - ArchDaily
articles.title: Sumayya Vally to Design Permanent Home for Elie Khouri Art Foundation in Dubai
articles.excerpt: Sumayya Vally of Counterspace has been appointed to design the permanent home for the Elie Khouri Art Foundation in Dubai's Jumeirah 1 district. Scheduled to open in late 2028, the repurposed residential property will host contemporary art exhibitions, education, and public programming.
articles.content:
The Elie Khouri Art Foundation has appointed Sumayya Vally of Counterspace to design its permanent home in Dubai, United Arab Emirates. Slated to open in late 2028, the institution will occupy a repurposed villa in the Jumeirah 1 district, transforming the existing property into a space for contemporary art exhibitions, education, and public programming. Architecture and curatorial programming are being developed in parallel.

Vally will lead the architectural transformation of the villa to incorporate galleries, educational spaces, pavilions, and a garden, while retaining the site's domestic character. The architectural concept draws on spatial references from Beirut street architecture and traditional Gulf courtyard houses. Elements such as the existing villa's doors, cornices, and room arrangements will inform a contemporary architectural language for public and cultural exchange.

Founded by French-Lebanese art collector and philanthropist Elie Khouri, the Foundation operates under the direction of Caroline Louca. Its programming will feature works from the collection, temporary exhibitions, institutional collaborations, loans, and learning initiatives. Counterspace approaches architecture through research into social histories, collective memory, and vernacular spatial practices.

articles.originalTitle: Italian Design Firm Henge Expands Into Tableware, Fragrances - WWD
articles.title: Italian Design Firm Henge Expands Into Tableware and Fragrances
articles.excerpt: Milan-based luxury furniture firm Henge has introduced its first collection of tableware, glassware, and home fragrances crafted from stone, glass, and metal.
articles.content: Italian luxury furniture maker Henge has expanded its portfolio into tableware, glassware, and home fragrances. The Milan-based company announced that its debut home collection relies on core materials such as stone, glass, and metal, featuring natural textures and hues. The collection includes Murano glass tumblers and a carafe designed by Ugo Cacciatori, alongside cast silver and gold trays by Yabu Pushelberg. Handcrafted in Carrara from Rouge Languedoc, Napoléon, and Gris Cévenol marbles, the Rever plates derive their name from the French word for dreaming. The brand also made its first foray into home fragrances with Henge Fragrance #34, named after its showroom at 34 Via della Spiga in Milan. The scent blends Calabrian bergamot, Sicilian lemon, and jasmine with notes of frankincense, Virginia tobacco, and Russian leather. This expansion aligns with an industry trend where high-end Italian design firms, including Molteni & C and Cassina, introduce smaller, more accessible design objects.

articles.originalTitle: Miami Beach Director and Mendes Wood DM founders on the fair's bold new changes - Art Basel
articles.title: Art Basel Miami Beach Implements Major Layout Changes for Its 24th Edition
articles.excerpt: Marking its 24th year, Art Basel Miami Beach is introducing a new floor plan and gallery configuration to improve navigation for collectors.
articles.content: Marking its 24th year, Art Basel Miami Beach is implementing substantial changes to its gallery lineup and floor plan. Fair Director Bridget Finn notes that feedback from exhibitors and the selection committee shaped the new footprint, designed to help collectors navigate the entire fair more easily and give presentations the attention they deserve. The new configuration features four symmetrical plazas instead of five, alongside redesigned entrances to improve navigation. Mendes Wood DM co-founders Matthew Wood and Pedro Mendes emphasize the fair's strong connection to Latin America and regional diversity. The gallery is bringing Rosana Paulino's first bronze sculpture, created for the Brazil Pavilion at the 2026 Venice Biennale, to the fair. Finn states that success is measured by the achievements of the participating galleries and the formation of new connections. Art Basel Miami Beach takes place from December 4 to 6, 2026.

articles.originalTitle: Edgar Degas | Promenade beside the Sea | L819 - The National Gallery, London
articles.title: Edgar Degas Painting Promenade beside the Sea at The National Gallery
articles.excerpt: Edgar Degas's early oil sketch Promenade beside the Sea, created around 1860 and depicting the Bay of Naples, is held at The National Gallery in London.
articles.content: Created around 1860 by Edgar Degas, Promenade beside the Sea stands as an early oil sketch exploring the recurrent theme of horses and riders. The artwork depicts an elegantly attired couple on horseback riding along a coastal route towards cliffs. A gentleman in black with a top hat and a lady sitting side-saddle in a dark riding habit make their way past coastal vegetation. The setting has been identified as the Bay of Naples, a location Degas visited during trips to see his Italian family. Open brushwork conveys the movement of the horses' gait, while impasto captures the energy of breaking waves. Measuring 22.5 by 32.5 centimeters, the oil on canvas is on long-term loan from the Gere Collection to The National Gallery in London, cataloged under inventory number L819. Evidence indicates the left-hand section derives from a notebook sketch housed in Paris. The composition reflects the artist's lifelong interest in movement and motion prior to the emergence of the Impressionist group.

articles.originalTitle: About the Constantinople to Istanbul: One City, Two Empires exhibition - Victoria and Albert Museum
articles.title: V&A Museum Explores Byzantine and Ottoman Legacy in Major Exhibition
articles.excerpt: The Victoria and Albert Museum is hosting Constantinople to Istanbul: One City, Two Empires, an exhibition exploring 1,600 years of artistic production from AD 330 to 1922.
articles.content: V&A South Kensington in London is presenting Constantinople to Istanbul: One City, Two Empires, an exhibition spanning the period from AD 330 to 1922. The exhibition examines the art and design traditions of both the Byzantine and Ottoman empires, highlighting their creative legacy that shaped the Mediterranean and beyond. Spread across four main sections, the exhibition features over 200 objects, including rare decorative arts, fine silks, textiles, ceramic tiles, mosaics, precious metalwork, jewelry, sculpture, architectural furnishings, manuscripts, and paintings. The first section, Roman Beginnings, explores the refounding of the city in AD 330 as the capital of the Roman Empire under Constantine the Great, focusing on its infrastructure and the Hippodrome. Heaven and Earth, the second section, explores how art and architecture served Christianity. Power and Reach examines how the Ottoman court projected authority through visual spectacle and luxury materials, while the final section, Life in the City, investigates the city's cosmopolitan character, religious coexistence, and 19th-century shifts in style. The exhibition remains open until 9 May 2027.

articles.originalTitle: Best Government/Public Building: Essex County Wynona Lipman Family Courthouse - Engineering News-Record
articles.title: Essex County Wynona Lipman Family Courthouse Wins Recognition
articles.excerpt: Built in Newark, the 266,000-square-foot, eight-story Essex County Wynona Lipman Family Courthouse consolidates previously dispersed family courts into a central location.
articles.content: Situated in Newark, the 266,000-square-foot, eight-story Essex County Wynona Lipman Family Courthouse consolidates previously dispersed family and children courts, probation services, and domestic violence units into a central urban location. The primary public entry is carved out under the upper floors to form a plaza as an extension of the streetscape. According to the submission, family courts require a de-escalating environment, addressed here by a multicolor art-glass two-story translucent screen on the public street wall and separate child-friendly playrooms in waiting areas. Constructing the massive complex in downtown Newark required meticulous coordination, including working within strict property lines, managing daily traffic flows, and minimizing disruptions to neighbors. The interior design divides spaces to separate hostile parties while accommodating sensitive zones, and integrates modern security with separate private entry points, holding cells, secure sallyports, and underground parking for judges. To counter unpredictable conditions, the project team relied on daily meetings and constant communication, allowing project managers, superintendents, and safety managers to address obstacles, coordinate daily tasks, and adapt in real time alongside cooperation with the city of Newark.

articles.originalTitle: Biennale Arte 2026 | Morocco Pavilion: DECLOSION - La Biennale di Venezia
articles.title: Venice Biennale 2026 Morocco Pavilion Announces Declosion Performance
articles.excerpt: Scheduled for the Arsenale during the 2026 Venice Biennale, the Morocco Pavilion will present the performance Declosion, drawing on the cosmology of Hesiod's Theogony.
articles.content: As part of the 2026 Venice Biennale, the Morocco Pavilion at the Arsenale will host the performance titled Declosion. Drawing from the chaos narrative in Hesiod's Theogony, the performance invokes Clotho, the figure who spins the thread of life. Engaging in a dialogue with Amina Agueznay's artwork, the event explores the cyclical rhythm of existence spanning birth, life, and death. Featuring performer Inès Abergel within the installation Asǝṭṭa, the work reveals the transition from emptiness to fullness and nonbeing to being. Artistic support for the performance is provided by Amina Agueznay, with music composition by Guilain Delanoue. Movement advisors include Alice Dardenne and Romane Piffaut, while scenography is advised by Amine Slimani and Federico Urso. Objects for the installation are crafted by Malika Benmoumen, Mahdia Anoufr, Koltoum Gaddem, Khaddouj Alja, and Florian SôngNguyen. The performance is scheduled for November 21, 2026, from 16:30 to 16:50.

articles.originalTitle: Lunchtime Lectures: Curating Urushi Now: Contemporary Japanese Lacquer - Victoria and Albert Museum
articles.title: Victoria and Albert Museum Hosts Curator Talk on Contemporary Japanese Lacquer
articles.excerpt: The Victoria and Albert Museum hosted a curator talk and display exploring the research and collection process behind contemporary Japanese lacquer art.
articles.content: The Victoria and Albert Museum presented a talk exploring the research and travel process behind the Urushi Now: Contemporary Japanese Lacquer project. Led by curator Masami Yamada, the event detailed the initiative funded by the Art Fund and Hiroyuki Maki. Spanning from northern Japan's urushi lacquer forests to artist studios nationwide, the project brings together works by 41 living artists, ranging from Living National Treasures to emerging talents. Hosted in the Toshiba Gallery of Japanese Art, the display highlights how artists are rethinking traditional materials through contemporary techniques. The resulting display remains open to visitors in Room 45 until April 30, 2027. Curator Masami Yamada also authored an upcoming publication on contemporary Japanese craft scheduled for release in the spring of 2027.

articles.originalTitle: Drop-in Design: Your Future City - Victoria and Albert Museum
articles.title: Designing the Future City Workshop at the V&A Museum
articles.excerpt: The Victoria and Albert Museum invites families and children aged 5 and over to design future public buildings using recycled materials in a free workshop.
articles.content: The Victoria and Albert Museum is hosting a hands-on town planning event for children and families in collaboration with architectural designer Jahba Anan and RIBA. At the V&A South Kensington, participants will imagine and redesign how schools, hospitals, libraries, and train stations might look in 2050. Drawing inspiration from the Design 1900–Now galleries, the program allows visitors to examine how design has transformed daily life over the past 125 years. Supported by the Adobe Foundation, attendees will use recycled materials to build mini models of their dream buildings and contribute them to a growing city model over five days. The free drop-in event is suitable for ages 5 and above, with all materials provided on-site. Visitors must ensure children are attended at all times. The venue offers comprehensive accessibility features, including baby-changing facilities, quiet spaces, and ear defenders available upon request from the Learning Centre Desk for families requiring sensory support.
